STEP 1 - Vessel type: shallow bowl (white, curved inner wall visible on the far side, food sits well below the rim, shadow inside). Actually the food mound is fairly high, but the bowl wall is short relative to its width, so treat it as a shallow-to-medium bowl; I use the shallow bowl formula.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a cereal/serving bowl, likely around 14-16 cm (cereal bowl) or larger.
b) Reference: the bowl's width spans roughly the same length as the wooden board's width (about 15 cm, since the board is a typical cutting strip). The bowl diameter is about 1.5 board widths... Using the board as the reference, the bowl spans roughly 0.85 of the board's visible width, so width ≈ 16 cm.
Reconciled width: 16 cm (cereal-bowl size, small-medium).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Yogurt/white creamy food (looks like plain yogurt or sour cream, a dense mound filling the bowl).
- Capacity (shallow bowl) = 0.2 x 16³ / 1000 = 0.2 x 4096 / 1000 = 0.82 L = 820 ml.
- Fill: the mound sits roughly level with or slightly below the rim, so fill ≈ 0.8 (depth fraction). Food volume = 820 x 0.8 x 0.8 = 525 ml.
- Bulk density of yogurt ≈ 1.0 g/ml (sauce/dairy class). Grams ≈ 525 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no visible base layer beyond the white mass; no separate item underneath.

STEP 5 - Plain yogurt: about 60-65 kcal per 100 g (whole-milk style; some Greek/sour cream would be higher, so I use ~90 kcal for a creamier, full-fat variety as a middle estimate).

Estimate: 525 g of creamy white food, roughly 500 g; energy ≈ 500 x 0.9 ≈ 450 kcal.

Result: a ~500 g serving of creamy white food (yogurt-like) in a ~16 cm bowl, about 450 kcal.
